summary: Market sentiment is broadly uneasy, with investors navigating a split between resilient economic data and escalating geopolitical tensions, as US weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows signal a robust labor market even as equity markets remain volatile. The primary macro drivers include rising Middle East instability, with Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia prompting Aramco to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters, pushing Citi to flag upside oil price risks while the US probes suspicious Iran oil trading, adding further supply-side uncertainty. At the sector level, AI and Nasdaq-linked tech stocks sold off sharply as investors rotated into defensives, though some analysts are selectively re-entering data center plays and defending Meta following its post-earnings decline, while Kering's Gucci posted another sales slip highlighting ongoing luxury goods weakness, and Dow Chemical beat profit estimates on pricing and cost discipline. The chief risk factors on investor radar include a potential oil supply shock stemming from Gulf conflict escalation, sustained pressure on high-multiple tech valuations amid a broader rotation, and geopolitical contagion risk should the Saudi-Yemen conflict intensify further. In the short term, markets are likely to remain choppy, with direction hinging on oil price trajectory, any de-escalation signals from the Middle East, and whether the strong labor market data can anchor confidence against the backdrop of sector rotation out of momentum-driven AI trades.
